name: Motivation & Autonomy
description: Concepts distinguishing intrinsic motivation (acting because the activity itself is valued) from extrinsic motivation (acting for an external reward), and the degree of choice a user feels they have over their own behaviour.

name: Goals & Progress
description: Concepts about how setting a visible target, and seeing measurable movement toward it, shapes effort — including the tendency to accelerate effort as a goal gets closer.

name: Loss & Ownership
description: Concepts about why losing something already held (a streak, a status, a collected set) is felt more strongly than gaining an equivalent new thing, often summarised as loss aversion.

name: Social Influence
description: Concepts about how visibility of others' behaviour, social commitments and comparison change an individual's own actions.

name: Learning & Reinforcement
description: Concepts from behavioural learning theory about how the timing and pattern of feedback or reward following an action affects whether that action is repeated.

name: Attention & Decision-Making
description: Concepts about how framing, personalisation and the salience of information affect what a user notices and how they decide what to do next.
